body.heading: Collect the clues
paragraphs: Weather presenters start with clues. Look at the clouds, feel the wind, and check whether the ground is wet or dry.
Draw today's weather on a big paper map: a sun, clouds, arrows for the wind. Your map is the presenter's most important tool.

body.heading: Present the show
paragraphs: Stand tall, hold your pretend microphone, and point to your map. Tell your audience what the weather is doing now and what it might do tomorrow.
Use presenter words: Today we can expect... Later on... Tomorrow will bring... A good guess is fine — real presenters use clever guesses too.

body.heading: Check your forecast
paragraphs: Tomorrow, look back. Did your forecast come true? Weather is tricky, and even real forecasts miss sometimes.
Keeping score of your guesses makes you a better forecaster, one show at a time.

takeaway: A weather presenter reads clues from the sky and turns them into a forecast — and checks it the next day.
safetyNotes: Only observe the weather from safe places — never go outside in thunder, lightning, or storms to check the sky.
screenFreeExtension: Present the report again in the morning and check whether yesterday's forecast came true.
